Seven Palestinians were killed in separate Israeli strikes throughout the day, Gaza’s civil defence rescue service said on Thursday.

Six of the seven were killed in various parts of Gaza City.

Two people were killed in a drone strike on a car, while one was killed in a drone attack on a tent in an encampment for displaced people, the rescue service and al-Shifa hospital said.

“Two people, a woman and a child, were killed and others were wounded when Israeli aircraft bombed a residential building” in Gaza City, the civil defence said.

A woman was also killed by artillery shelling in Gaza City, health officials reported.

The civil defence reported that "one person was killed by Israeli fire southeast of Deir al-Balah in central Gaza".

Over 1,800 people missing in Yemen since July, Red Cross says

The International Committee of the Red Cross (ICRC) said that it received more than 1,800 missing persons reports in Yemen since the renewed fighting began in July. 

"The recent escalation of hostilities in Yemen has left countless families in anguish. Since July 2026, we have received over 1,800 tracing requests from families looking for missing loved ones," it said in a statement posted on X. 

"Families of the missing have the right to know the fate and whereabouts of their loved ones. Behind every missing person is a family living in anguish. Their pain cannot be ignored, and their wait must not be prolonged," said Christine Cipolla, head of ICRC's Yemen delegation.

item.title: [www.middleeasteye.net] Huckabee top aide modified and suppressed US embassy reporting critical of Israel: Report
item.description:
Huckabee top aide modified and suppressed US embassy reporting critical of Israel: Report

A top aide to US ambassador to Israel Mike Huckabee has repeatedly altered or suppressed embassy reporting that would have been critical of Israeli activities in the occupied West Bank and Gaza Strip, according to a New York Times investigation.

David Milstein, 36, has blocked, rewritten or delayed reports to Washington about illegal Israeli settlement expansion in the occupied West Bank, Israeli settler violence, and the killings of nine Palestinian Americans, the NYT reported, citing US officials familiar with his work.

The newspaper said it interviewed 15 US officials who had worked with Milstein, including many in Washington, as well as nine former diplomats. They were all cited anonymously for fear of reprisals.

The NYT also reviewed dozens of internal documents, including diplomatic cables, memos and other communications.

The investigation found that Milstein's interventions raised concerns among embassy staff and Washington officials that information reaching the US government was being distorted. Several officials told the NYT that Milstein's interventions surpassed those of any recent predecessor.

The sources told the paper they were concerned that Milstein was undermining diplomatic work and even contradicting US President Donald Trump's policies.

Read more: Huckabee top aide reportedly modified and suppressed US embassy reporting critical of Israel

item.title: [www.middleeasteye.net] 'Global Day of Action' for Palestine will see mass protests in dozens of countries this weekend
item.description:
'Global Day of Action' for Palestine will see mass protests in dozens of countries this weekend

Submitted by Mera Aladam on Fri, 10/09/2026 - 03:58
The mass pro-Palestine protests on Saturday will take place across 60 countries in over 250 locations worldwide
Protestors attend a pro-Palestinian demonstration on the third anniversary of Israel's genocide in Gaza, in Berlin, Germany on 7 October 2026 (Christian Mang/Reuters)
Off

Capital cities across the globe will see major protests and actions in support of Palestine on Saturday, the Global Alliance for Palestine (GAFP) has announced. 

According to the statement, more than 200 organisations will be mobilising for a mass "synchronised Global Day of Action", involving civil society groups, trade unions, student federations and human rights networks across 60 countries.

The global event is organised by GAFP alongside the Anti-Apartheid Movement (AAM) and Global Coalition Against Occupation of Palestine (SANED).

"As governments actively fund, arm, and protect Israel from any legal accountability, grassroots movements are refusing to allow this genocide to become normalised as the status quo," GAFP wrote. 

It added that the event "marks a decisive shift, moving beyond symbolic protest toward direct civil intervention to shut down public complicity and demand systemic accountability for Israel’s war crimes and genocide".

Anas Altikriti, secretary-general of the Global Alliance for Palestine, said that the third anniversary marking Israel's continued genocide in Gaza is a "stark, devastating reminder of the unbearable terror and suffering that the Palestinian people have been forced to endure every single day for three years".

"As world powers remain silent and complicit, civil society is rising," he added, saying that the global demonstration is a a direct response to "this ongoing horror".

Altikriti went on to describe the event as a "declaration that the global conscience will not stand idly by as a genocide is normalised."

Our interactive map shows the scale and diversity of this weekend’s Global Day of Action for Palestine. More than 300 actions across 60+ countries, united around two demands: End the Genocide. Defend the Land. Explore the map: https://t.co/bvAZtd6PQw https://t.co/OIvoQ5lZWv

— Global Alliance For Palestine (@ga4palestine) October 7, 2026

"We are taking to the streets to demand total accountability, an immediate end to the siege, and a free Palestine."

Demand for Palestinian liberation, end to genocide

GAFP stressed that the global mobilisation on Saturday is "not a passive memorial for three years of genocide", but is instead a "direct action to halt the machinery that enables Israel's violence".

Three years of death and devastation: Israel's war on Gaza in pictures
Read More »

Participating organisations in over 250 locations worldwide are expected to shut down civic squares, encircle government buildings and blockade corporate entities directly tied to military supply chains.

"The objective is clear: render normal commerce and political diplomacy impossible while Israel’s genocide continues uninterrupted."

As well as mass protests in major capitals worldwide, in cities like Athens and Modena, the coalition indicated that "actions will extend across multiple days with cultural sit-ins, public teach-ins, and large-scale visual projections highlighting Israel’s war crimes directly onto government and corporate buildings".

"Three years into Israel's genocide, the global movement for Palestine has grown in power, unity, and resolve," the statement added.

"As the October 10 Global Day of Action approaches, millions around the world across every continent are sending an unmistakable message: the demand for Palestinian liberation, land protection, and an immediate end to Israel's genocide and occupation will no longer wait on international permission - it is taking to the streets to enforce it."

Pakistani premier condemns Houthi attacks on Saudi Arabia

Pakistani Prime Minister Shehbaz Sharif condemned recent Houthi attacks targeting Saudi Arabia, including strikes on Riyadh's King Khalid International Airport, which resulted in casualties. 

"I commend the vigilance and professionalism of the Saudi armed forces and the Coalition in intercepting multiple ballistic missiles and their tireless efforts to protect innocent lives and safeguard the Kingdom," he said in a post on X.

He added that Islamabad stands in "unwavering solidarity" with the kingdom, vowing to the commitment of Saudi Arabia's "sovereignty, territorial integrity and security", in line with their recent Mecca Joint Defense Agreement.

"We also fully support Saudi Arabia’s legitimate right to defend its people and protect its cities and vital infrastructure," Sharif said. 

"The Houthi militia must immediately cease these attacks. We will continue to stand shoulder to shoulder with Saudi Arabia in the face of these threats."

item.description:
Iranian lawmaker says Tehran not seeking production of nuclear weapons

Iranian lawmaker Alaeddin Boroujerdi indicated that Tehran is not aiming for the production of nuclear weapons after remarks made by US Vice President JD Vance.

Speaking to NourNews agency, Boroujerdi said that Iran's nuclear programme is pursued  according to the nuclear Non-Proliferation Treaty.

Iran’s enrichment activities are unrelated to the US, and Washington should focus on fulfilling its own obligations regarding nuclear arms reduction," he said.

Earlier, Vance said that Iran must make a "meaningful" reduction in its nuclear enrichment capacity to satisfy US demands and end the war. 

"If you don't want a nuclear weapon, then why do you need 60 percent enriched fuel? And if you want to show commitment to not building a nuclear weapon, don't build highly enriched fuel. That's a very basic threshold issue," Vance said during an interview with Reuters.

Vance also indicated that the US remained open to an agreement but would require concrete Iranian nuclear concessions. "We're not going to trade words for actions," he said.

item.title: [World news | The Guardian] Labour fends off Green party to win Holborn and St Pancras byelection
item.description:
Victory by Sagal Abdi-Wali in north London seat will reassure Andy Burnham in high-stakes battle for left of British politics

  • Holborn and St Pancras byelection – live updates

Labour has seen off the Greens to win the Holborn and St Pancras byelection in a result that will reassure Andy Burnham and dent Zack Polanski’s position as a decisive power player on the left of British politics.

The byelection, called after the former prime minister Keir Starmer resigned from the seat in September, was considered a two-horse race between the Labour candidate, Sagal Abdi-Wali, and the Green party leader, Polanski. Abdi-Wali received 12,292 votes, 45% of the vote, to Polanski’s 8,928, 33% of the vote.

item.title: [www.middleeasteye.net] US lost or damaged 81 aircraft in Iran war, Congress report estimates
item.description:
US lost or damaged 81 aircraft in Iran war, Congress report estimates

At least 81 US military aircraft, including fighter jets and drones, have been lost or damaged during Operation Epic Fury, Washington’s military campaign against Iran, according to a report released Monday by the Congressional Budget Office (CBO).

The nonpartisan agency estimated that the cost of aircraft losses stood between $1.9bn and $3.3bn as of 1 August. 

The report adds to the growing financial toll of the US-Israeli war on Iran, which began on 28 February and has continued into its eighth month without a lasting ceasefire.

item.description:
Four killed in attacks on Riyadh airport, Saudia confirms employee’s death

Three Saudi citizens were killed in two separate attacks on Riyadh airport, while several people of other nationalities sustained injuries ranging from minor to serious, Saudi Arabia's Civil Aviation Authority said. 

The first attack targeted airport facilities and the second struck a Saudi Airlines aircraft, the authority added.

Saudi Arabia's national airline said one of its employees was killed in Thursday's attacks against King Khalid International Airport in Riyadh, which also left an aircraft on the ground damaged.

Saudia added that the aircraft had no passengers on board and that flights and airport operations resumed on Thursday.

item.title: [World news | The Guardian] Hurricane Isaias ‘biggest test’ for Fema since Trump cuts, experts warn
item.description:
Gulf officials say they are ready for storm but concerns raised about restructured agency’s ability to respond effectively

Gulf state officials say they are prepared for Hurricane Isaias, but the storm could be the first major test of Fema’s ability to deploy a large surge workforce after the Trump administration’s sweeping cuts and restructuring of the agency, emergency management experts say.

The Trump administration has said it wants to eliminate, or drastically downsize, Fema, putting more burden on states. More than 4,300 employees left the agency in fiscal year 2025, about 17% of the workforce, according to a recent US government accountability office (GAO) report. The agency’s staffing reductions were not carried out systematically to ensure Fema could still meet its statutory obligations, said Chris Currie, director of homeland security and justice at the GAO.

Maliki said Houthi attacks on civilians and civilian facilities “will be met with resolve”.

item.title: [www.middleeasteye.net] Yemen’s deputy defence minister says forces advancing on multiple fronts
item.description:
Yemen’s deputy defence minister says forces advancing on multiple fronts

Yemen’s deputy defence minister, Major-General Samir al-Sabri, has said that the Houthi-held capital, Sanaa, remains a direct military target for government forces, Al Jazeera reported. 

Sabri said control of the Bab al-Mandeb strait and Yemen’s western coast was crucial because of their strategic importance and links to regional and global affairs. 

The timing of an advance and the need to cross areas near the city are among the factors affecting the operation, he said. 

Attention remained focused on Hodeidah, Sanaa and Saada, he said, adding that the government forces had “great momentum”.
